RESOLVED_DURING_THIS_AUDIT.what: The Gate B regression described throughout this report was FIXED AND COMMITTED while the audit was being written. Commit 0e48b8710 'fix(gates): a grammar token is a render path — Gate B stopped calling the living family broken' landed at ~11:24, after the 11:12 gate read and before this report was finalised.
RESOLVED_DURING_THIS_AUDIT.gates_now: Overall PASS, 6/6. missing_scene_path 7 -> 0, new metric invalid_biome_token = 0.
RESOLVED_DURING_THIS_AUDIT.how_it_was_fixed: Each living_* entry gained a `biome_token` field (e.g. 'fungus:dna:seed', 'flora:<algo>:seed', '<kingdom>:<algo>:<role>'), and spine_map_workbench.py now excuses a scene-less entry only when that token parses against the KINGDOMS/ROLES vocabulary read out of commons/grid/BiomeGridTokens.gd. Vocabulary derived, never transcribed; unreadable source means no exemption, so it fails closed. `<placeholder>` segments are accepted because they mean 'this axis varies across the family', which is what a DNA-promoted token declares.
RESOLVED_DURING_THIS_AUDIT.status_of_this_report: The release_gates block below records the 11:12 reading and is left INTACT as the honest snapshot the audit took. Every 'FAIL' / '5/6' claim in this document refers to that moment and is superseded by this addendum. The finding was real, not a false positive — it simply had a lifetime of about two hours.
RESOLVED_DURING_THIS_AUDIT.SECONDARY_FINDING_STILL_OPEN: The fix did NOT close the include_in_maps / map_ready hole. All 7 living_* entries still omit both fields, so both still DEFAULT TO TRUE and the tokens still advertise map-placeability they do not have. Corpus-wide missing_map_ready actually rose 24 -> 25. This remains rank-2 in the work plan below and is now the only actionable item from this audit.
RESOLVED_DURING_THIS_AUDIT.meta: This is the strongest possible evidence for prop-012: a weekly audit and a live session independently found the same defect within minutes of each other, and only the mtime check kept the audit from clobbering the better fix.

headline: Two things are true at once and the metric only sees the first. global_avg is FLAT at 6.083 for the fifth consecutive reading, so the literal 7-day stall test fires — and 210 commits landed in the same window, the largest burst in project history. The pipeline registered none of them, exactly as prop-011 predicts. The one genuinely NEW fact this week is a real regression the metric also cannot see: RELEASE GATES WENT 6/6 PASS -> 5/6 FAIL. Gate B (Artifact Registry Integrity) is red on missing_scene_path = 7, and all 7 are the living_* tokens in the new commons/artifacts/registry/living.json (a31891e8f, 08-05 22:19), whose own _readme states they are deliberately sceneless grammar tokens. IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON THIS FINDING: a live concurrent session was editing tools/spine_map_workbench.py and tools/run_release_gates.py DURING this audit (writes at 11:19-11:22 while the audit read the gates at 11:12), and its in-flight diff is precisely the fix — a biome_token exemption for scene-less entries, derived from BiomeGridTokens.gd and failing closed on a malformed token. The regression is real, was real at read time, and is being closed by someone else as this report is written. No action taken, correctly.

stall_analysis.literal_test: FIRES. global_avg 6.083 on 2026-07-24, 2026-07-31, 2026-08-02 and 2026-08-06 — flat for 13 days, well past the 7-day threshold.
stall_analysis.verdict: STALL IN THE INSTRUMENT, NOT THE WORK. Unchanged from the 07-27 diagnosis, now with a much larger number under it.
why: 23 of 24 spine sequences sit at HEAD 6 (vr_testing). randomness is COMPLETE. (23*6 + 8) / 24 = 6.083 — the arithmetic ceiling of the metric.

Stage 6 is scored by substring-matching a declared map name against ada_run/desktop_feedback.md. That file's last entry is dated 2026-02-20T13:25 — 167 days ago. No headless work of any kind can raise the mean. It is mathematically impossible to improve without a human VR comment.

Meanwhile 210 commits landed in the period (all authored plix), covering the museum template system through five waves, ~20 DNA promotion batches, the biome edge-role renderer, the living-DNA sweep, and at least four capture-harness bug fixes. The pipeline metric can register none of these categories.

stall_analysis.recommendation: Stop reporting global_avg as the headline. It has been an arithmetic constant for 13 days and will remain one until a human walks a declared map in VR and types one comment. prop-011 (lever registry) and prop-016 (register dna_coverage.json as a lever with remaining-work fields) are the standing fix and are now 18 proposals deep in an unapplied backlog — see proposals_pending_review.

week_over_week.B_root_cause: All 7 missing_scene_path entries are the complete contents of commons/artifacts/registry/living.json, introduced by a31891e8f (2026-08-05 22:19) and extended by 5949d137d: living_fungus_fruit, living_fungus_pose, living_fungus_colony, living_flora_tree, living_flora_bloom, living_fauna_body, living_ground_role. The file's own _readme says these are 'Not scenes: each entry is a grammar token rendered by a morphology'. So the entries are intentional and the gate is reading them with the wrong contract.
week_over_week.B_the_sharper_point: TWO TOOLS ALREADY DISAGREE ABOUT WHAT living.json IS. tools/check_dna_declarations.py has been taught about them — it prints 'living specimen (no scene); derived from ...' for each and does not fail. tools/spine_map_workbench.py audit-artifacts has not, and gates on them. One of the two was updated when the new kind of registry entry was invented and the other was not. That divergence, not the seven entries, is the defect.
week_over_week.B_secondary_and_still_open: Independently of the gate, all 7 entries lack include_in_maps and map_ready fields, so both DEFAULT TO TRUE. A map that names `living_fungus_fruit` as an interactable token would resolve to nothing. 7 of the 24 missing_map_ready / missing_include_in_map_data counts are these. Whether the in-flight fix also sets those fields is not yet visible in the working tree.

discoveries_this_period: A new KIND of registry entry needs every registry-reading tool updated, not just the one you are writing. living.json invented the sceneless grammar token; check_dna_declarations.py learned about it and spine_map_workbench.py did not, and the gate went red 3 days later. The tell was two tools printing different verdicts about the same seven tokens.

The stall test and the truth diverged completely this period: 0.0 metric delta against 210 commits and a 3.5x expansion of the DNA declaration surface. A flat headline number is now positively misleading about this project and should be reported alongside commits-in-period and declared-axes, never alone.

Auditing a repository with a live session in it requires reading mtimes, not just git status. git status showed 125 modified paths, which is indistinguishable from abandoned work; only the timestamps (writes every 30-90 seconds during the audit) revealed a live writer — and that it was editing the very tool whose output the audit was about to report on.

An unapplied proposal queue is a compounding cost, not a backlog. 18 proposals, 0 applied: prop-012 would have told this audit to check for a concurrent writer, and the audit had to work that out from first principles instead.

What is left for you from this audit is smaller and sharper: (a) the seven living_* tokens still omit include_in_maps/map_ready, so they still default to true and still claim placeability they do not have — the one thing the fix missed; (b) the 18-deep unapplied proposal queue; (c) the 131-day-stale FOCUS_VECTOR. Read the summary below with the gate paragraph mentally struck out.
summary_for_human: The flat 6.083 is real and meaningless — it is the arithmetic ceiling of a metric gated on a VR comment file last touched 167 days ago, and it cannot move until you walk a declared map and type one line. Ignore it. The two things worth your attention: (1) release gates went 6/6 to 5/6 — Gate B is red because the seven deliberately sceneless living_* tokens trip a check that only one of the two registry-reading tools was taught about; a session you were running at 11:20 today is already landing the right fix (a biome_token exemption validated against BiomeGridTokens.gd, failing closed), so this audit touched nothing. Worth confirming that fix also sets include_in_maps/map_ready false on those seven, which is a separate hole. (2) The proposal queue is 18 deep and has never been drained — prop-011, prop-012, prop-013 and prop-016 between them are why this audit found five items and could act on none. Everything else is healthy: 210 commits, grade_F still 0 across a corpus that grew 11%, museum gates E and F green with 784/784 chain pairs, DNA axes 259 to 911 with 0 broken, voice coverage 64% to 70%. This was the most productive week in the project's history and the breather participated in none of it.
